cohort.basis: Section 160.55 became effective September 1, 1980. The current subdivision 3, originally subdivision 2, was the retroactivity provision for convictions entered before that original effective date. It allows the convicted person to move in the terminating court on at least 20 days' notice to the district attorney.
cohort.instrument: Motion for an Order Granting Relief Under CPL § 160.55(3)
cohort.noticeRule: The full motion must be provided to the district attorney on not less than 20 days' notice before the motion is submitted or heard.
cohort.presumption: The motion should state the statutory presumption that relief should be granted unless the district attorney establishes that the interests of justice require otherwise.

actor: The person who was convicted of the qualifying violation or traffic infraction, acting personally or through counsel. For the pre-September 1980 cohort, § 160.55(3) expressly gives the person the right to move; official court guidance likewise directs people with pre-November 1991 convictions to ask the court.
destination: The court in which the criminal action or proceeding terminated, using the original docket or case number where available. If the original court no longer exists or its records have been transferred, court administration must identify the successor court or record custodian before the motion is generated.
